attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He states it directly as his view, not as a quotation.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence: no one yet knows how to build syntax-driven compositional semantics. The 'what one needs' part is normative framing. The contract rightly treats it as context and scores only the factual part.

contract.note: The plain reading is general, reliable compositional understanding of ordinary language, not restricted parsers. That is how an informed reader would take it given the Imagen and deep-understanding context. It is fair, but the result depends on that breadth reading.

evidence.note: COGS (2020) shows weak, unstable compositional generalization in specific neural models. It also notes that rule-based parsers compose by design. It covers particular models before the snapshot date, so it can't settle the state of the whole field.

Feb 2022: compositional parsers (LeAR, AM parser) generalize structurally on COGS. That success is on a restricted synthetic benchmark, which the contract says is not enough to contradict. It shows neither field-wide absence nor broad reliability.
2020 framework showing that compositionality takes several distinct tests. It is background only and says nothing about whether a method existed in May 2022.

reviews.rationale: None of the items amounts to the comprehensive assessment needed for support. None documents reliable composition across varied ordinary language, so none contradicts. e2's success is on a restricted benchmark, and e1 and e3 cover specific models or methods. The packet does not settle the field's state on 2022-05-28.
